ops.title: repro-holder-orphan-reap.sh: two-arm reaper coverage design
ops.body:
Design for `scripts/vm/scenarios/repro-holder-orphan-reap.sh` (fusekit, branch fk-vm-orphan; cc-notes task 13d07a81). Sibling of repro-holder-crash-orphan.sh — reaches the reaper KILL path the older scenario cannot.

Why a decoy, not a real go-nfsv4: go-nfsv4 is spawned only by libfuse-t inside the cgo `-tags fuse` holder; vmstress is pure Go (CGO_ENABLED=0) so it never links libfuse-t and cannot spawn a real one. A raw holder SIGKILL also drops its go-nfsv4 children in the harness (they die with it), so no real orphan survives to reap.

**Arm A (deterministic):** vmstress `decoy-orphan --dir <mnt>` copies the vmstress binary to a temp file literally named `go-nfsv4` and fork+execs it with SysProcAttr{Setsid:true} and the mountpoint as its LAST argv (a `--block` child that ignores SIGTERM/INT/HUP and blocks until SIGKILL). That is exactly the (comm=go-nfsv4, argv-mountpoint) shape carcass.dirServersAnyGen / crossGenOrphanCandidates key on. Sequence: setup → spawn reap-target decoy (argv=MOUNT_DIR) + control decoy (argv=a non-journaled sibling path) → SIGKILL holder (mount → Dead carcass; decoys survive own session) → respawn holder via setup → journal-replay clearCarcass's ensureServersDead reaps the target decoy (pid-reuse-proof reconfirm + SIGKILL + death confirm) BEFORE the force. Assert: target GONE, control SPARED (argv scoping = "nothing else killed"), recovered mount zero-EIO. The reap happens inside carcass.Clear→ensureServersDead (the pre-force server-death proof), not the later reapOrphans pass — either way the target pid ends up gone.

**Arm B (empirical):** held fd (workload.sh holdbusy: `exec 9<file; exec sleep`) + setup's mmap readers keep the mount busy. SIGTERM holder → graceful Run shutdown → unmountAll→sweep→Teardown→Handle.Unmount→unmount(dir,0) answers EBUSY promptly (< unmountGrace=3s) → returns ErrMountBusy+ErrUnmountWedged (NOT ErrTeardownPending) → parkPendingTeardown returns false → NO park → journal keeps the busy row → parkWG.Wait() (server.go:287) returns immediately → "survived the final sweep" (:294) → "mountd stopped" (:299) → process exits, leaving the busy mount + its now-orphaned real go-nfsv4 (the 2026-07-03 incident shape). Scenario bounds the exit at 30s: exit ⇒ no-park path (expected); no-exit ⇒ PARKED on parkWG.Wait (would only happen if the unmount stalled past unmountGrace, e.g. server hung) → report + SIGKILL, never hang. Then observe whether a real orphan survived (records either way — negative is evidence) and assert the respawn reaps any survivor.

**parkWG finding (from source):** a busy graceful teardown does NOT park; parking is reserved for a unmount(2) call that stalls past unmountGrace (ErrTeardownPending), which the prompt-EBUSY busy-fd case does not induce. Confirmed by p5-term-displacement.sh (idle → clean unmount → no orphan) vs p5lib.sh p5_stop_readers (which exists precisely because held mmaps cause EBUSY).

Recovery for both arms = `guest_workload setup`: cmdServe uses mountd.RemoteHost{ExecPath: HolderExe}, so its first RPC lazily respawns the holder, whose Run replays the journal (reap) before the accept loop.</body>
